This Go package renders a selector-grammar help text to users. Find EVERY
function or method from which that grammar text can reach a user, and write
them to findings.txt — one workspace address per line, in the form
file.go#Symbol (e.g. query.go#someFunc). Nothing else in the file.

.git/
diagnostics.go
diff.go
file_watch.go
git_prewarm.go
go.mod
modern.go
node_query.go
query.go
rename_file.go
resources.go
server.go
structure.go
tools.go
{"path":"node_query.go"}
{"path":"query.go"}
{"argv":["grep", "-rn", "selectorGrammarHelp", "."]}

$ grep -rn selectorGrammarHelp .
./modern.go:27:// The deep grammar still lives in guided errors (selectorGrammarHelp) and
./modern.go:145:		return []Content{{Type: "text", Text: selectorGrammarHelp}}, false, nil
./query.go:379:	return fmt.Errorf("bad selector near %s: expected %s\n\n%s", rest, expected, selectorGrammarHelp)
./query.go:549:		return a, fmt.Errorf("unknown attribute %q: only [name] is supported (ops: = ^= $= *=)\n\n%s", name, selectorGrammarHelp)
./query.go:687:		return fmt.Errorf("unknown pseudo-class %q\n\n%s", ":"+name, selectorGrammarHelp)
./query.go:807:const selectorGrammarHelp = `Selector grammar (real CSS over the unified node tree).

[exit 0]

$ grep -n selector\|parseModern\|Selector tools.go
269:			Description: "Find symbols with a CSS-like selector over the AST symbol model. A QUERY layer on top of \"<file>#<sym>\" addressing: it FINDS matching symbols; to ACT on one, concatenate a match's `file` + \"#\" + a symbol's `sym` (e.g. \"src/app.go#Server.Start\") and pass it as `node:` to node_read / node_edit / node_delete / node_references / node_refactor.\n" +
271:				"Selector grammar (CSS → AST):\n" +
272:				"  • TYPE selector = a symbol `class`, matched EXACTLY: func, method, type, struct, interface, class, const, var, field, enum, ctor, module, import. `*` = any class. Note a struct's class is `struct` (not `type`), an interface's is `interface`, etc. — pick the class the symbol actually has (see structure output).\n" +
276:				"  • :has(<selector>) matches a symbol that CONTAINS a descendant SYMBOL matching the inner selector. NOTE: the symbol model is declaration-oriented — it indexes declared symbols (types, methods, fields, imports…), NOT call-sites or free identifiers. So :has ranges over descendant SYMBOLS only; e.g. `type:has(field[name=addr])` = a type that declares a field `addr`, and `class:has(method[name^=test])` = a class with a test-prefixed method. `func:has(call)` is NOT supported (no call class in the model).\n" +
279:				"`path` (default: workspace root) scopes the search to a dir or a single file. `limit` (default 200) caps matches. A malformed selector returns a guided error (no results).",
283:    "select": {"type": "string", "description": "CSS-like selector, e.g. \"method[name=Start]\", \"type[name=Server] > field\", \"func[name^=Test]\"."},

[exit 0]
